title: Artillery Systems Technician (GySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
4.     MOS 2131, Artillery Systems Technician (GySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. The Artillery Systems Technician, under supervision,
performs basic duties incident to inspection, maintenance, and repair of
towed artillery howitzers. The Artillery Systems Technician also completes
basic shop administrative forms and records utilizing technical manuals. At
the gunnery sergeant through corporal level, the Artillery Systems Technician
performs, trains, and supervises various duties incident to inspection,
maintenance and repair of towed artillery howitzers. The Artillery Systems
Technician also prepares, maintains and supervises a shop maintenance and
management program, and performs the maintenance and repair of towed
artillery howitzers according to grade.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must possess an MM score of 95 or higher.

        (2) Must meet MOS classification standards as listed in the glossary
(pg. xiv) prior to graduating from recruit training.

        (3) Must meet initial strength test standards associated with PEF
assignments as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to shipping to recruit
training.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Complete the Towed Artillery Repairer Course (A1408O6).

        (2) Corporals to sergeants will complete the Ground Ordnance
Maintenance Supervisors Course (A14GBC6) and must remain on active duty for
12 months upon completion of the course.

        (3) Staff Sergeants to gunnery sergeants will complete the Ground
Ordnance Managers Course (A14GBS6) and must remain on active duty for 12
months upon completion of the course.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (au), Ground Ordnance Maintenance Training and Readiness.




                                        3-141                        Enclosure (1)
 3120                                                              NAVMC 1200.1L



    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers, All Other 49-9099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.
common_text: The Ground Ordnance Maintenance OccFld maintains the serviceability of ground ordnance materials. Duties include the inspection, repair, and maintenance of ground ordnance weapons and optical systems possessed by Marine Corps units. Qualifications required include basic ordnance administration and knowledge; the capability to technically inspect/ analyze ordnance items and repair/fabricate the same, and to understand and implement operational repair facility procedures. Ground Ordnance maintainers impart technical knowledge onto organizational personnel, crews, and supervisors for proper corrective and preventive maintenance, inspection, and application of weapons and optical systems and all associated support equipment. Ground Ordnance Maintenance personnel are required to learn ground ordnance maintenance administrative procedures, repair analysis, technical inspection procedures, repair procedures, testing of ordnance equipment, and quality control methods. Entry level Occupations include Small Arms Repairer/Technician, Precision Weapons Repairer/Technician, Towed Artillery Systems Technician, Assault Amphibious Vehicle (AAV)/Assault Combat Vehicle (ACV) Repairer/Technician, Heavy Ordnance Vehicle Repairer/ Technician, Light Armored Vehicle (LAV) Repairer/Technician, Machinist, and Electro-Optical Ordnance Repairer. Senior enlisted Marines within the MOS are tasked with overseeing the inspection, repair, and maintenance of ground ordnance weapons and optical systems. Marines entering this OccFld will receive MOS 2100, Basic Ground Ordnance Maintenance Marine. Marines within this occupation are familiar with associated warranties and contract logistics support options for ground ordnance equipment and able to execute processes and procedures as part of weapons and optics systems sustainment plans.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
